The result applies after seed removal; it does not directly transfer an arbitrary seeded or controlled word. It also supplies no joint limit in which depth or angles change with $D$ or $n$. [OpenAI (2026b), §2, “Fixed-word transfer”][q-transfer]. For an ordinary cost or mixer the root updates are, respectively, $$ u\longmapsto e^{-itZq(v_Z)}u, \qquad u\longmapsto e^{-i\beta X}u, \qquad v_Z=u^*Zu\,\mathrm{vac}. $$ The source proves smooth convergence for these updates, their adjoints and fixed angle derivatives. The resulting occupation bounds supply the hypothesis of the root-shift energy proposition in §8.1. Thus its energy is the scaled edge limit required for transfer. Finally merge consecutive gates of the same type and insert zero-angle gates where needed to express $W$ in alternating QAOA form. [OpenAI (2026b), §2, “Ordinary root updates”][q-ordinary-updates].

rows.label: strip-recovery
rows.text:
The curvature argument needs estimates uniform over the approximating
coefficients. Here is the route from the control formula to those estimates;
all bounds are taken on a fixed strip ending before time one.

For finite-step coefficients and a smooth, even, convex, one-Lipschitz
terminal function $\psi$, the evolution through a step of height $c$ is
$$
\Phi(t,x)=
\begin{cases}
c^{-1}\log P_{b-t}(e^{c\Phi(b,\cdot)})(x),&c>0,\\
P_{b-t}\Phi(b,\cdot)(x),&c=0,
\end{cases}
$$
where $P_h$ denotes convolution with a centred Gaussian of variance $h$.
The heat formula preserves evenness, convexity and the spatial Lipschitz
bound. Along a controlled path $dY_s=\gamma(s)\alpha_s\,ds+dB_s$, the drift
of the value minus the accumulated control cost is
$-\gamma(s)(\alpha_s-\Phi_x(s,Y_s))^2/2$. It is nonpositive, and is zero
for the feedback control. This proves the stated control formula for the
smooth step problem, including attainability by its feedback diffusion.

Using the same control in two such problems and then taking suprema gives
$$
\|\Phi_{\gamma,\psi}-\Phi_{\widetilde\gamma,\widetilde\psi}\|_\infty
\le \|\psi-\widetilde\psi\|_\infty
       +\frac32\|\gamma-\widetilde\gamma\|_{L^1(0,1)}.
$$
The drift part costs at most the coefficient difference in $L^1$, by the
terminal Lipschitz bound; the quadratic cost contributes another half of
that difference. The supremum norm is of the difference of the values,
which is bounded even though each value grows linearly in $x$.
With $\psi_M(x)=M^{-1}\log(2\cosh Mx)$,
$0\le\psi_M-|x|\le(\log2)/M$. Choose simultaneously $\gamma_m\to\gamma$ in $L^1$ and $M_m\to\infty$.
These are two distinct requirements: $M_m\ge\|\gamma_m\|_\infty$ alone
does not force terminal convergence. This compatible approximation
determines a unique uniform limiting value. Its terminal bound,
given in §2.2, also follows directly: choose the zero control for the lower
bound, and use $|\alpha|-\alpha^2/2\le1/2$ for the upper bound.

To obtain spatial derivatives, choose $T<b<1$. Monotonicity gives the
uniform coefficient estimate
$$
\gamma(t)\le\frac{\|\gamma\|_1}{1-b}\quad(0\le t\le b).
$$
An $L^1$-convergent family thus has a common coefficient bound $\Gamma$ on
this larger strip. For its smooth step approximants, put $U=\Phi_x$.
The differentiated mild equation is
$$
U(t)=P_{b-t}U(b)+\int_t^b\gamma(s)P_{s-t}[U(s)U_x(s)]\,ds.
$$
Since $\|U\|_\infty\le1$ and
$\|\partial_xP_hF\|_\infty\le Ch^{-1/2}\|F\|_\infty$,
$$
\|U_x(t)\|_\infty\le\frac C{\sqrt{b-t}}
 +C\Gamma\int_t^b\frac{\|U_x(s)\|_\infty}{\sqrt{s-t}}\,ds.
$$
Substituting this inequality once into its own integral uses
$\int_t^s((r-t)(s-r))^{-1/2}\,dr=\pi$. It reduces the estimate to an
ordinary backward Gronwall inequality with integrable forcing. This bounds
$U_x$ uniformly on $[0,T]$ without any terminal derivative bound. Repeating
on successively smaller strips bounds each higher spatial derivative: put
one derivative on the heat kernel and the rest on $UU_x$; only the term
$U\partial_x^mU$ contains the new highest derivative. The remaining products
have already been bounded.

Uniform convergence of the values then yields convergence of every
positive spatial derivative. For a bounded twice differentiable difference
$F$ with bounded second derivative, Taylor's formula gives
$$
\|F'\|_\infty\le \frac{2\|F\|_\infty}{h}
                         +\frac h2\|F''\|_\infty\qquad(h>0).
$$
First choose $h$ small using the common second-derivative bound, then make
$\|F\|_\infty$ small. Iterate on derivative differences. Passing to the
integral form of the differentiated PDE proves local absolute continuity
in time and its almost-everywhere equations. No classical time derivative
at a coefficient jump, and no derivative of $|x|$ at its cusp, is being
assumed.

Finally, couple all feedback diffusions with the same Brownian motion.
On $[0,T]$, let $L$ be a common spatial Lipschitz bound for their drifts.
The difference of the two integral equations gives, for example,
$$
\sup_{s\le T}|X_s^n-X_s|
\le e^{LT}\left(\|\gamma_n-\gamma\|_1
 +\|\gamma_n\|_1\|u_n-u\|_{\infty,[0,T]\times\mathbb R}\right)
 \longrightarrow0.
$$
This is a deterministic bound under the coupling. The derivative bounds
one order higher ensure uniform continuity when derivatives are evaluated
at these moving points. Every fixed polynomial in the bounded derivatives
therefore converges in expectation. This is precisely the convergence
needed for the integrated curvature expression in §4; none of the forward
density scores or their quotients need converge.
[OpenAI (2026a), Lemmas 2.1–2.3][fs-reg].

rows.label: targets
rows.text:
Write $u=\Phi_x$, $a=\Phi_{xx}$, and
$dX_t=\gamma(t)u(t,X_t)\,dt+dB_t$, $X_0=0$.
Write $q(t)=\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]$ for the second moment of this
gradient along $X$.
The first result assumes an admissible minimizer. It constructs its
Stieltjes measure and an associated diffusion, proves
$\operatorname{supp}\mu_\gamma=[0,1)$ and strict increase of $\gamma$,
and obtains $\mathbb E u(t,X_t)^2=t$ and
$\mathbb E a(t,X_t)^2=1$ for every associated diffusion. The selected
formal statement has exactly this conditional scope; it does not assert a
smooth density.
Its [Lean implementation at the fixed source revision][support-main] implements the
[separately stated formal challenge][support-type]. The
[Comparator configuration][support-config] identifies the intended
comparison; the evidence retained with this draft does not establish
a successful research-target replay.

The second result concerns the scalar value. A bounded martingale ends
at a spin-valued random variable whose Brownian correlation represents
$P_*$. Finite Gaussian coefficients approximate that correlation at each
fixed $T<1$, followed by $T\uparrow1$. Its formal statement is separate
and retains the minimizer and diffusion hypotheses where needed. The QAOA
theorem goes further: for each requested accuracy it selects one finite
deterministic circuit, independent of size and disorder, whose limiting
expected energy approaches $P_*$. Neither formal statement asserts that
circuit conclusion.
The scalar clauses are in a [separate Lean implementation][value-main], with their
own [formal challenge][value-type] and [Comparator configuration][value-config].
Those links identify the selected statements, not a completed replay
receipt for either research target.

rows.label: value
rows.text:
**Proposition 6.1 (terminal value).** For the minimizer and diffusion of
Theorem 5.1 there is a spin-valued terminal variable $U_1$ such that
$u(t,X_t)=\mathbb E[U_1\mid\mathcal F_t]$ and
$$
P_*=\mathbb E[U_1B_1]=\int_0^1\mathbb E a(t,X_t)\,dt.
\tag{6.1}
$$
Its finite-cutoff tail lies in $[0,1-T]$. This proposition uses the
attained Parisi formula in addition to the support theorem.

The bounded martingale $u(t,X_t)$ converges almost surely and in $L^2$
to $U_1$. Its second moment tends to one because $q(t)=t$.
Since $|U_1|\le1$, $\mathbb E U_1^2=1$ forces $U_1^2=1$ almost surely.
Uniform integrability identifies $u(t,X_t)=\mathbb E[U_1\mid\mathcal F_t]$,
which is the conditional-expectation identity used below.

The drift bound $|\gamma u|\le\gamma\in L^1$ gives convergence of $X_t$
to $X_1$. Uniform terminal convergence of $\Phi$ to $|x|$, together
with convexity, gives $u(t,x_t)\to\operatorname{sgn}(x)$ when
$x_t\to x\ne0$. Thus $U_1X_1=|X_1|$, including when $X_1=0$;
no proof that this event has probability zero is needed.

Itô's formula gives
$$
\mathbb E\Phi(t,X_t)=\Phi(0,0)+\frac12\int_0^t\gamma(s)s\,ds.
$$
The terminal limit first gives
$\Phi(0,0)=\mathbb E|X_1|-\tfrac12\int_0^1s\gamma(s)ds$.
Subtracting the second half from the definition of the functional yields
$\mathcal P(\gamma)=\mathbb E|X_1|-\int_0^1s\gamma(s)\,ds$.
The ground-state Parisi formula identifies this with $P_*$.
The diffusion equation, conditional expectation and Fubini give
$$
\mathbb E[U_1X_1]=\mathbb E[U_1B_1]
 +\int_0^1\gamma(s)\mathbb E[u(s,X_s)^2]\,ds.
$$
Bounded $u,U_1$ and integrable $\gamma$ justify these terms.
Combining the identities and using stochastic integral covariance gives
$$
P_*=\mathbb E|X_1|-\int_0^1t\gamma(t)\,dt
 =\mathbb E[U_1B_1]=\int_0^1\mathbb E a(t,X_t)\,dt.
$$
The last integral is absolutely bounded by one because
$\mathbb E|a|\le(\mathbb E a^2)^{1/2}=1$.
Full support supplies $\mathbb E a^2=1$, whereas the value uses
$\int\mathbb E a$. Substituting the second moment into the value identity
would change the assertion. [OpenAI (2026a), §7][fs-cons].
The prediction error and the energy tail have different sizes:
$$
\|U_1-u(T,X_T)\|_2^2=1-T,
$$
$$
P_*-\int_0^T\mathbb E a(t,X_t)\,dt
=\mathbb E[(U_1-u(T,X_T))(B_1-B_T)]\in[0,1-T].
$$
The first identity is orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal F_T$.
Martingale orthogonality removes the past Brownian component in the
second; Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the product by $1-T$, and convexity
makes it nonnegative. No uniform terminal curvature bound is needed.
The stochastic value calculation has a direct antecedent in
[Sellke, arXiv:2105.03506v4, Definition 1.3 and Lemma 3.11](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03506v4).
There, “optimizable” means the contact identity $\mathbb E u(t,X_t)^2=t$
on $[q,1)$, with $q$ the infimum of the support of the coefficient
function. Lemma 3.11 derives the finite-cutoff value identity by applying
Itô's formula to $\Phi$ and $xu$, before taking the terminal limit.
This is the same value-recovery mechanism used here, specialized to
zero field and $\xi''=1$.

A cutoff must retain the full Parisi penalty. Set
$\Psi(T,x)=\Phi(T,x)-xu(T,x)$ and
$I(T)=\int_0^T\mathbb E a(t,X_t)\,dt$. Subtracting the complete penalty
from the finite-time Itô identity gives
$$
\mathcal P(\gamma)-I(T)
 =\mathbb E\Psi(T,X_T)
  +\frac12\int_0^T\gamma(t)(q(t)-t)\,dt
  -\frac12\int_T^1t\gamma(t)\,dt.
$$
Under contact the middle term vanishes. The final term is absent from
the displayed equality in [El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke,
arXiv:2001.00904v1, §6.2, pp. 32–33][eams20]. Its sign is nonpositive,
so the upper bound by $\mathbb E\Psi(T,X_T)$ used there remains valid;
its magnitude tends to zero by integrability. This finite-cutoff
correction is consistent with the exact terminal identity above.

rows.text:
The source collection retains the two manuscripts, formal statements,
their implementations and build metadata. The derived project specifies
Lean 4.34.1 and a pinned mathlib revision. The proof-assistant and library
infrastructure is described by [de Moura and Ullrich (2021), *The Lean 4
Theorem Prover and Programming Language*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-79876-5_37)
and [The mathlib Community (2020), *The Lean Mathematical Library*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3372885.3373824).
These references credit the software; the retained project metadata identifies
the versions used for this source. The retained polynomial computation
in §4 uses exact rational arithmetic. Its expansion matches
all 22 positive remainder
coefficients. The surplus of the $v^4$ coefficient above $1/1000$ is
$140507/1521000000$. This finite check does not establish the PDE
signs, integrability, boundary flux or limiting argument.

The source-byte audit verified the inspected edition; it did not prove
its claims. Paper assembly checked identifiers, declared scope and
document bindings, not semantic correspondence or reader understanding.
Tool-compatibility checks and synthetic fixtures exercised their stated
cases, not either selected SK theorem. Reading of the mathematical and
formal sources supports the bounded comparisons reported here, without
a complete independent proof acceptance or transitive axiom audit.

The retained observations must be kept separate. The original graph records
unrun plans and an earlier full-support attempt that could not start
because the Comparator executable was unavailable. A later retained
attempt, observed on 23 October 2026, built and exported the challenge,
then stopped while building the implementing solution. The retained
[partial-observation receipt](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/21b1f9e995c4276fdad02377b378f11541a3d5e9/examples/qaoa-sk/verification/full-support-build-failure-20261023.json)
and [log](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/21b1f9e995c4276fdad02377b378f11541a3d5e9/examples/qaoa-sk/verification/full-support-build-failure-20261023.log) preserve that event: the imported
object for `Diffusion/AbsIncrement` was missing. The challenge is an
admitted specification, so its successful build and export are not a
proof of the theorem. There was no successful solution export or
research-target comparison in that observation.

The scalar-value invocation in the same original two-target run reached
a terminal failure observed on 24 October 2026. Its challenge built and
exported, but its solution build stopped because the imported object for
`Gaussian/IntegralPositiveMulGaussian` was missing. The retained scalar
receipt and log establish no solution export, kernel acceptance or
comparison acceptance. The companion source review locates both records.
Both failures concern the original build configuration. A subsequent
repair to the derived configuration was recorded. In the subsequent
corrected replay, the full-support challenge built and its exporter was
observed running. Reconciliation on 25 October found that the controller
had stopped without a recovered terminal research result. At that date,
Comparator and research extraction outcomes were unknown, neither
rejected nor accepted. The [interruption receipt](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/21b1f9e995c4276fdad02377b378f11541a3d5e9/examples/qaoa-sk/verification/corrected-replay-interruption-20261025.json)
retains this observation separately from the original build failures.

A subsequent [source-bound observation of 26 October 2026](https://wcook04.github.io/lean-exposition-site/verification/full-support-build-extraction-observation-20261026.json)
records a successful local Lake build of the Support implementation and
v2 extraction of the single conditional full-support root. Its selected
traversal contains 1,674 declarations. The root reports no sorry, unsafe
or partial flag, and its recorded transitive axiom names are
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The selected in-scope
traversal completed, but dependencies outside it remain unresolved
boundaries; the extracted graph is partial. This does not establish
minimiser existence, positive density, the scalar target or QAOA convergence.

The portable observation identifies the original receipts by their hashes
and retains the source inventory, root and extraction limits. Its
internal-consistency checks are not authenticated execution provenance.
The curated paper graph records the build and documentary extraction
observation separately; it is not the extracted declaration graph.
Comparator acceptance, standalone kernel replay and the scalar-target
results remain pending. The earlier failed and interrupted invocations
remain dated history, rather than evidence of a later rejection or
acceptance. Permitted axioms and checker settings describe the requested
comparison; they cannot supply its missing result.

This editorial revision does not establish a new formal result.
The [source review through 26 October 2026](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/ef46d0e72787c1dc283733b10b433d112f97ac64/papers/qaoa-sk/source-review/references-and-adversarial-review.md)
records the preceding paper revision's reading coverage, finite checks,
unsuccessful observations and remaining obligations; viewing it requires
repository access. This remains a draft after source-based agent review;
independent mathematical acceptance and a human reconstruction study
have not been performed.

rows.label: weighted-tree
rows.text: **Source comparison for the finite weighted-tree formula.** This is an auxiliary check of the positive-temperature route. Readers continuing the circuit argument can go directly to [§11.1.1](#temperature-route-comparison) or [§11.2](#fixed-word-probability). The comparison here is with [El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke, arXiv:2111.06813v2, 3 February 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06813v2). Proposition 2.1 (p. 7) sums the adjacent-time term over $\ell=2,\ldots,L$. Applying Lemma 4.3, equation (4.6) (p. 14), replaces the expectation in that summand by the coefficient at $r=\ell-1$, so the resulting range is $r=1,\ldots,L-1$. The displayed ranges in (4.5) (p. 13) and (4.18) (p. 16) are instead $2,\ldots,L$. Separately, the same-time display (2.21) in Lemma 2.8 (p. 9) omits a factor $1/k$ that is present in its proof and in Proposition 2.1. The QAOA manuscript's Appendix A already uses the latter proposition, the reindexed sum and spatial Lipschitz bounds for both $a$ and $b$. The two following calculations establish the finite discrepancies and their precise scope. They do not compare formulae in the journal edition. **The test weights expose the missing factor.** Work on the $k$-regular tree, $k\ge2$, and let all initial labels $g_i$ be independent standard Gaussians. In particular, the adjacent vertices $o,v$ have distinct labels $g_o,g_v$. Set $u_i^0=u_{i\to j}^0=g_i$, $A_{i\to j}^{-1}=1$, and use constant algorithmic update functions $F_r=H_r=1$. These satisfy EAMS Assumption 2 and its later boundedness Assumption 3. For the auxiliary tests in Lemma 2.8 choose $Y_o^r=g_o$ and $\widetilde Y_v^r=g_v$ for every $r\ge0$. Each test is measurable with respect to its required initial-label sigma-field, and all moments are finite. The tests are separate from the constant update functions. At $t=1$, the recursion gives $$ u_o^1=k^{-1/2}\sum_{x\sim o}g_x,\qquad u_v^1=k^{-1/2}\sum_{y\sim v}g_y. $$ Hence $$ \mathbb E[u_o^1u_v^1g_og_v] =\frac1k\sum_{x\sim o,\,y\sim v}\mathbb E[g_xg_yg_og_v] =\frac1k. $$ Only $x=v,y=o$ survives. The printed right side of (2.21) is $\mathbb E[g_v^2g_o^2]=1$; multiplying it by $1/k$ agrees with the calculation. Both initial labels matter. With both test weights equal to one, both sides are zero; with just the neighbouring test omitted, the left side is an odd Gaussian moment and is again zero. A bounded version uses $Y_o^r=\operatorname{sgn}(g_o)$ and $\widetilde Y_v^r=\operatorname{sgn}(g_v)$. Only the same edge pair survives, so $$ \mathbb E[u_o^1u_v^1\operatorname{sgn}(g_o)\operatorname{sgn}(g_v)] =\frac1k(\mathbb E|g|)^2=\frac{2}{\pi k}, $$ whereas the printed right side is $2/\pi$. These tests are bounded and initial-label measurable. Both witnesses concern the auxiliary weighted identity; neither substitutes arbitrary test weights into a Parisi output theorem. **The shifted endpoint violates the printed uniform finite bound.** For a separate test retain the initial labels and set $$ \delta=\varepsilon=\frac14,\qquad L=2,\qquad b(t,x)=0, \qquad a(t,x)= \begin{cases} 1,&0\le t<3/8,\\ -1,&3/8\le t<1. \end{cases} $$ Use the source's actual initial states $x_i^0=x_{i\to j}^0=\sqrt\delta\,g_i$ and its definitions $A_{i\to j}^r=a(r\delta,x_{i\to j}^r)$, $B_i^r=a(r\delta,x_i^r)$. The state initialization has not been set to zero; it drops out of these coefficients because $a$ is independent of $x$. This fixed function is bounded by $K=1$, has spatial Lipschitz constant zero, and satisfies $a^2=1$, so all directed-edge normalizers are exactly one. The drift has Lipschitz constant $M=0$, and $L\delta=1/2\le1-\varepsilon$. It therefore meets the printed hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 and Assumptions 2–3. That finite theorem does not require temporal continuity or positivity of $a$. At the mesh points, $a_0=a_1=1$ and $a_2=-1$. Thus $$ u_i^2=\frac1{\sqrt{k(k-1)}} \sum_{w\sim i}\sum_{y\sim w,\,y\ne i}g_y, \qquad z_i^2=\sqrt\delta\,(u_i^1+u_i^2). $$ The equal-time covariances across the edge are zero. Each adjacent-time covariance is $\sqrt{k-1}/k$: exactly $k-1$ labels occur in both sums, and their product normalization is $k\sqrt{k-1}$. Therefore $$ k\mathbb E[z_o^2z_v^2]=2\delta\sqrt{k-1},\qquad \frac{k}{2\sqrt{k-1}}\mathbb E[z_o^2z_v^2]=\delta. $$ The target printed in (4.5) uses $a(2\delta,x_o^2)=-1$, so it is $-2\delta\sqrt{k-1}$. Its absolute error is $4\delta\sqrt{k-1}$, which is unbounded as $k\to\infty$ while all arguments of the claimed constant $C(M,K,\delta,\varepsilon)$ remain fixed. This refutes auxiliary Theorem 4.1 as printed. The example is not a Parisi curvature: it changes sign. Consequently it is not by itself a counterexample to the specialized assertion (4.18) in Proposition 4.7; the endpoint correction there comes from the exact proposition and reindexing explained above. Neither test refutes the main EAMS Theorem 1.7. **A finite estimate with the required hypotheses.** The source argument does provide a usable replacement. Fix $\delta>0$, $L\ge1$ and $L\delta<1$. Allow the coefficients $a_k,b_k$ to depend on degree, but require bounds independent of $k$ at the finitely many mesh times: $|a_k|\le K$ with $K\ge1$, and spatial Lipschitz constants $L_a,L_b$ for $a_k,b_k$. Use the original initialization and the same normalized function for node and directed-edge coefficients, with $\mathbb E(A_{i\to j}^r)^2=1$. Then $$ \left|k\mathbb E[z_o^Lz_v^L] -2\sqrt{k-1}\,\delta\sum_{r=1}^{L-1}\mathbb E B_o^r\right| \le C(K,L_a,L_b,\delta,L). $$ The constant is independent of $k$, and the sum is empty when $L=1$. The coefficient expectation on the right uses the vertex law; its normalization was defined using the directed-edge law. The following proof keeps the two laws distinct. It reconstructs the finite estimate from EAMS Proposition 2.1 and Lemmas 3.2–3.4 and 4.2–4.3; it is not a claim that changing an index alone repairs every hypothesis of the printed theorem. Put $D=k-1$. Conditional on the earlier cavity labels, the new message is centered Gaussian with variance $(\tau^r)^2$. Its recursion is $$ (\tau_{i\to j}^{r+1})^2=\frac1D \sum_{\substack{w\in\partial i\\w\ne j}}(A_{w\to i}^{r-1})^2(\tau_{w\to i}^r)^2, \qquad \tau^0=1. $$ This conditional Gaussianity gives $\Delta_r=\mathbb E[((\tau^r)^2-1)^2]\le V_r/D$, where $$ V_0=0,\qquad V_{r+1}=2K^4V_r+2(K^4+1). $$ Indeed, split the conditional-variance recursion into the average of $(A^{r-1})^2((\tau^r)^2-1)$ and the average of $(A^{r-1})^2-1$. Jensen bounds the first square, while independence of child cavities and exact coefficient normalization bound the second by a constant over $D$. The moment recursion also gives $\mathbb E(u_{i\to j}^r)^2\le K^{2r}$. Splitting off the missing neighbour as in the source gives $\mathbb E|u_i^r-u_{i\to j}^r|^2\le4K^{2r}/k$. Subtract the node and directed-edge Euler recursions. Their equal initial states and the drift Lipschitz bound give $$ \mathbb E|x_i^r-x_{i\to j}^r|^2\le d_r/k, \quad d_0=0,\qquad d_{r+1}=2(1+\delta L_b)^2d_r+8\delta K^{2(r+1)}. $$ The bound $\|B_i^r-A_{i\to j}^r\|_2\le L_a\sqrt{d_r/k}$ now uses spatial Lipschitzness of $a$. This property is invoked in the proof of EAMS Lemma 4.2 but omitted from the printed hypotheses of Theorem 4.1; it is available in the QAOA manuscript's compact-strip application. For $s=\ell-1$, the adjacent-time summand of Proposition 2.1 is $$ Q_s=\mathbb E[A_{v\to o}^{s-1}(u_{v\to o}^s)^2B_v^{s-1}B_o^s]. $$ Let $\mathcal G_{i\to j}^{r,+}$ be the labels within distance $r$ of $i$ in its cavity after removing edge $ij$. Condition on $\mathcal G_{v\to o}^{s-1,+}\vee\mathcal G_{o\to v}^{s,+}$. The three coefficient factors are measurable there: their vertex balls split into these two disjoint cavity balls. The newest layer driving $u_{v\to o}^s$ is outside this field; adding the initial label at $v$ to the source's minus field does not change the conditional law, since that message and its variance exclude that label. Conditioning therefore replaces $(u_{v\to o}^s)^2-1$ by $(\tau_{v\to o}^s)^2-1$. Its contribution is bounded by $K^3\sqrt{V_s/D}$. Replacing the two node coefficients by directed-edge coefficients then costs at most $K^2L_a(\sqrt{d_{s-1}}+\sqrt{d_s})/\sqrt k$. The two directed-edge trees are independent; exact normalization reduces their product expectation to $\mathbb E A_{o\to v}^s$. One final comparison with $\mathbb E B_o^s$ proves $$ |Q_s-\mathbb E B_o^s|\le\frac{C_s}{\sqrt D},\quad C_s=K^3\sqrt{V_s}+K^2L_a\sqrt{d_{s-1}} +(K^2+1)L_a\sqrt{d_s}. $$ For the same-time remainder in that proposition, $|R_\ell|\le K^{2\ell+2}$ by boundedness and Cauchy–Schwarz. Hence the asserted finite bound holds, for example, with $$ C=2\delta\sum_{s=1}^{L-1}C_s +\delta\sum_{\ell=1}^LK^{2\ell+2}. $$ No constant uniform in increasing horizon, temperature or terminal cutoff has been asserted. **Why the continuum value survives the correction.** The QAOA manuscript already checks the convergence and uniform boundedness of its finitely many degree-dependent normalizers, and supplies both spatial Lipschitz bounds, before taking the degree limit. Its limiting coefficient $m_r=c_{\delta,r}\mathbb E a(t_r,X_r^\delta)$ satisfies $|m_r|\le1$ by Cauchy–Schwarz and the definition of $c_{\delta,r}$. The shifted and corrected sums differ exactly by $$ \delta\sum_{r=2}^Lm_r-\delta\sum_{r=1}^{L-1}m_r =\delta(m_L-m_1),\qquad |\delta(m_L-m_1)|\le2\delta. $$ Thus the error in the printed unnormalized finite theorem can grow like $\sqrt{k}$ at fixed mesh even though the correction disappears in the subsequent normalized continuum limit. The fixed-temperature coupling and separate strong realization in the QAOA manuscript justify that limiting application. These checks neither reject nor independently certify the whole EAMS or QAOA theorem. [OpenAI (2026b), Appendix A][q-positive].
